[1/4] Plan: durable checksummed claim-ledger store with backup and quarantine recovery

impact_assessment.why: ClaimLedger roundtrips as JSON but has no file API, so verdicts and kill-test evidence are lost when the process exits. The open-ended evidence loop needs a durable claim store.
impact_assessment.benefits: save_ledger writes one checksummed snapshot atomically (temp+fsync+replace) with a .bak of the previous snapshot; load_ledger restores it, quarantines a corrupt primary and falls back to .bak; verify_ledger_file names missing/checksum/schema defects; a lock serialises writers and steals stale locks.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claims_store.py module only, no agent API change; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock with 30s stale steal and bounded timeout; state: new local snapshot/.bak/.lock files, not committed.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep ClaimLedger as the data model; verify schema/checksum/claims on load; write temp+fsync+replace with 5 retries and a .bak; test roundtrip, backup fallback, tamper, schema, stale lock, fresh-lock timeout, deterministic checksum and no temp leftovers; rerun 282 tests and AIKit.

[1/4] Plan: append-only checksummed calibration forecast journal for cross-run scoring

impact_assessment.why: calibration.summary scores only the forecasts present in one process; SelfModel.calibration() reads the current episode lists. Forecasts are immutable observations but vanish on exit, so cross-run Brier/skill cannot be computed.
impact_assessment.benefits: append_forecasts validates and appends one checksummed JSONL record per forecast under a writer lock; load_forecasts restores them; verify_forecast_file names corrupt/duplicate records; two runs aggregate to 10 resolved forecasts and a stable Brier/skill.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new calibration_store.py module only, no agent API change; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock with 30s stale steal and bounded timeout; state: new local JSONL/.lock files, not committed.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep scoring in calibration.summary; enforce unique ids and schema/checksum per line; append under the lock with fsync and dir fsync; test roundtrip, two-run aggregation, duplicates, tamper, corrupt line, missing, stale/fresh lock and invalid inputs; rerun 293 tests and AIKit.

[1/4] Plan: opt-in SelfModel forecast bridge into the calibration journal

impact_assessment.why: The persistent SelfModel records confidence/outcome pairs and the calibration journal can store them, but no logged run connects the two: real-run forecasts stay in memory and vanish on exit, so cross-run calibration needs hand-built records.
impact_assessment.benefits: run_task_logged(calibration_path=...) appends only the current run's forecasts after the verdict, under a header-digest prefix; a default T3:15 run stays 13 in-memory forecasts with no file, the logged run persists 13/13 with the same Brier 0.230769, and a second run appends only 6 new records (19 total, two prefixes).
impact_assessment.risks: contract: SelfModel forecast_count/forecasts and run_task_logged calibration_path; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: calibration_store lock; state: new local journal append after the verdict, opt-in.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Fail fast without a persistent SelfModel/forecast API; capture the pre-run count and slice only that run; prefix ids with the header digest; test default/logged/two-runs/missing/corrupt/actions; rerun 314 tests and AIKit.
